oil.when: 2010–2014 (accelerator pedal method; 2014 also lets you use SET/CLR)
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition on with the engine off.
Slowly press the accelerator pedal fully to the floor and release it three times within five seconds.
Turn the ignition off, then start the car. If the CHANGE ENGINE OIL SOON message comes back, the reset did not take: repeat the steps.
oil.note: Checked in the 2010 Getting to Know Your Camaro guide and the 2014 owner's manual. On 2014 cars you can also show REMAINING OIL LIFE on the driver display and press and hold SET/CLR.

oil.when: 2016 redesigned Camaro (SEL button or accelerator pedal)
steps: Reset only after the engine oil and filter have actually been changed.
Bring REMAINING OIL LIFE up on the driver information display.
Press and hold SEL while oil life is showing, until it changes to 100%.
Or: with the ignition on and the engine off, press the accelerator pedal fully to the floor and release it three times within five seconds.
Start the car and make sure the CHANGE ENGINE OIL SOON message is gone.
Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the Tire and Loading Information label below the driver's door latch.
There is no reset button. The low tire pressure light stays on until the pressure is corrected, then goes off on its own.
tpms.note: If the light comes on only on cold mornings and goes off as you drive, a tire is getting low: check and top up the pressures. If the tire pressure light flashes for about a minute when you start the car and then stays on, the warning system itself has a fault. A reset won't fix it; have it checked.
